mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6.0% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous and persistent rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong and sustained increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals improved consumer purchasing power, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both UNRATE and PAYEMS below their 12-month averages in the same month signals a broad-based labor market weakening, which reduces aggregate demand and corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both fall below 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
